You have been accommodating. The family has withdrawn its interest in certain people. We were never interested, officially.

— Brandt-Marrow
does.subject: Withdrawn

does.text:
Understood. Some files will take a few days to find; they are being found now, by people I trust, and some of them will not be found at all. The family has outlasted eleven governments. We expect to make it twelve.

— Brandt-Marrow

opening.text:
Your friend has the Treasury. How brave. The arrangements will continue to run themselves, as they did under my grandmother and will under my niece; your friend will find the books balance without anyone quite knowing why. I remain at court, naturally. One does.

— Brandt-Marrow, lately of the Treasury
opening.subject: From the corridor

characters.name: Yusuf Adeyemi-Lark
characters.bio: An auditor by temperament and a believer by upbringing; was a magistrate on a frontier bench until he noticed where the frontier's money went. Has never taken a gift, including birthdays. Reports what he finds, to whoever is supposed to hear it, and then to everyone else.
characters.fear: Finding the ruler's name in them.

letters.appointed:
Thank you. I should tell you what I am before you regret it. I audit. I will audit the Treasury, the ministries, the fleet's yards and the Foreign Office's gifts, and when I find a colleague with their hand in the state's pocket I will tell you, in the brief, in writing. If you keep them after I have told you twice, I will tell the gazette and leave. I do not say this to threaten. I say it so you can plan.

— Y. Adeyemi-Lark, Treasury

loyal: I audit. I am telling you now so it is not a surprise later.
The books balance and they are honest, which is rarer. I checked both.
Clean ledgers this month. I would like to say that every month; help me say it.
cooling: The books balance. There is a column I cannot explain and a colleague who can but will not.

loyal: More worlds than offices means more ledgers than auditors. I am not asking for worlds. I am asking for auditors.
The reserve is low and I know where every credit of it went. That is small comfort; it is the only comfort I have.
The Clan's terms are honest and ruinous. I would rather a ruinous honesty than a comfortable lie. Take it only with the repayment written on the wall.
The company wants a subsidy. I have read their books. Read them yourself before you sign; page nine.
Sanctions on {target}. There will be smugglers. I will audit them too.
Approved. I will account for every credit of it, and you will see the account.
Declined. The ledger notes it. The ledger notes everything.
Unanswered. I have filed it. I file everything; it is my only vice.
Understood. The audits are in the safe. The safe has one key and it is on your desk.
I cannot audit a government that keeps what I find. I resign, and the gazette has the file.
Good morning. I checked the overnight ledgers. They are honest. Enjoy it.

does.text:
Understood. The audits are in the safe; the safe has one key and it is on your desk. Read the file marked 'colleagues' before you appoint my replacement. It is short, and it is about them.

— Adeyemi-Lark

opening.text: A colleague is taking money. The file is on your desk. Act, or I will say it again louder.

One of your ministers is taking money; I have the ledger and the dates and I have put both on your desk. I will not name them in a letter the corridor can read. I will name them in the brief, which you read. Act on it and we need never speak of it again.

— Adeyemi-Lark
opening.subject: A colleague

does.subject: My resignation
does.text:
I reported it twice and the minister is still in the chair. I cannot audit a government that keeps what I find. I resign the Treasury, and the gazette has the file, because somebody should read it.

— Yusuf Adeyemi-Lark

The column I could not explain is gone. I assume you acted. Thank you; I will not ask how.

— Adeyemi-Lark
does.subject: Gone

does.text:
Understood. The audits are in the safe; the safe has one key and it is on your desk. Read the file marked 'colleagues' before you appoint my replacement. It is short, and it is about them.

— Adeyemi-Lark

opening.subject: Honest books
opening.text:
You act on the audits. I have served two governments that did not and one that did, and this is the one I will stay with. The Treasury's competence rises when its minister sleeps; I have started sleeping.

— Adeyemi-Lark

does.text:
Understood. The audits are in the safe; the safe has one key and it is on your desk. Read the file marked 'colleagues' before you appoint my replacement. It is short, and it is about them.

— Adeyemi-Lark

opening.text:
Your friend has the Treasury. I have kept the audits. I will keep auditing; I cannot help it, and someone should. If your friend's books do not balance I will tell you, and if they balance for the wrong reasons I will tell you that too. I am not loyal to chairs. I am loyal to columns.

— Adeyemi-Lark, lately of the Treasury
opening.subject: From the corridor

characters.name: Sable Quist
characters.bio: Designed the orbital yards on a frontier world and came to the capital angry about how slowly it builds. Has no patience for theory, mysticism, or cabinet. Keeps a stopwatch on her desk and uses it on meetings.

letters.appointed:
I build yards. You have put me in a chair, which is not a yard, so I will say what I want and then go back to work. Fund the industrial line: hull alloys, drive tolerances, yard automation. Not the drive theory; theory is for people with time. Not the Enlightenment; that is mysticism with a budget. Ships, faster. Give me a season and I will give you a yard that lays a cruiser in half the time.

— S. Quist, Academy

loyal: I build yards. This is not a yard. I will make it one.
The yard line is on schedule. On schedule is the only compliment I give.
Steady. I distrust steady; steady is what a yard does before it slips.
cooling: The industrial line was cut for a theory line. Theory does not lay hulls.
brutus: The faculty want a minister who signs things. I have begun signing things.

loyal: Fund the industrial line. The theory line is beautiful and the hulls do not care.
cooling: Pick what you like. I will tell the yards it was strategic.

loyal: You cannot build that hull yet. Give me a season on the alloys and you can.
The Enlightenment bid. Mysticism with a budget. I will fund it because you asked; I will not pretend to understand why.
cooling: Transcendence. I would rather have a yard. I have said so.

loyal: {target} is transcending. Fine. While they meditate, we build. Fund the yards.
Worked stone on {world}. Interesting. Does any of it hold a tolerance?
An explosion in the test bay. Within tolerance. The tolerance was generous.
We lost. Was it the hulls? If it was the hulls, I want the wreck.
Approved. The yard starts tonight; I have the shift already rostered.
Declined. The yard idles. Yards hate idling; so do I.
Unanswered. I ran the stopwatch. Forty days.
Dismissed. Good. The yards are on the frontier and so, now, am I.
brutus: Dismissed. The yard crews know who got them the alloys.

loyal: I resign. A yard somewhere needs me more than this chair does.
Morning. The yards ran all night. I was in one.

does.text:
Dismissed. Good; I was not built for chairs. The yard crews on the frontier know who got them the alloys, and they will build for me whoever owns the yard. Keep that in mind when the company comes asking.

— Quist

opening.text: Two proposals, no yard. I have the stopwatch running.

Two industrial proposals, two silences, and the stopwatch says forty days. I am not a patient person; that is why the yards work. Fund the line or tell me to go back to the frontier, where things get built.

— Quist
opening.subject: The stopwatch

does.subject: My resignation
does.text:
Ninety days on the stopwatch and no yard. I resign the Academy; there is a frontier yard that lays hulls faster than this court signs them, and I would rather be there.

— Sable Quist

Dismissed. Good; I was not built for chairs. The yard crews on the frontier know who got them the alloys, and they will build for me whoever owns the yard. Keep that in mind when the company comes asking.

— Quist

opening.subject: A yard
opening.text:
You funded the line. The yard lays a cruiser in half the time now; come and watch, it is the only beautiful thing I know. I will stay in the chair as long as it keeps building.

— Quist

does.text:
Dismissed. Good; I was not built for chairs. The yard crews on the frontier know who got them the alloys, and they will build for me whoever owns the yard. Keep that in mind when the company comes asking.

— Quist

opening.text: You sold a yard to a company. My yard. The crews will build for whoever I tell them to.

You have chartered a company over the yards I built. Companies build for shareholders and shareholders do not launch ships. I will stay in the chair for the alloys' sake, but the crews are mine, and if this court ever moves I will know which way the yards face.

— Quist
opening.subject: My yard

does.text:
The charter is revoked. The yard is a yard again. We will not speak of it.

— Quist
does.subject: A yard again

does.text:
Dismissed. Good; I was not built for chairs. The yard crews on the frontier know who got them the alloys, and they will build for me whoever owns the yard. Keep that in mind when the company comes asking.

— Quist

Dismissed. Good; I was not built for chairs. The yard crews on the frontier know who got them the alloys, and they will build for me whoever owns the yard. Keep that in mind when the company comes asking.

— Quist

opening.text:
Your friend has the Academy. I have gone back to the yards, which I should never have left. I will keep sending the alloy specifications to whoever sits in the chair; make sure your friend can read a tolerance. Most cannot.

— Quist, lately of the Academy
opening.subject: From the corridor

characters.name: Veles Tamar
characters.bio: Science as scripture: for the Archon, the Enlightenment is not a project but the reason there is a state at all. Brilliant, serene, and entirely without scruple about who gets there first, provided it is not someone else.

letters.appointed:
You have given the Academy to a believer, which is the only kind of scientist worth the chair. Everything we build, every fleet and foundry, is scaffolding for one thing: the crossing. I will propose the bid when the programme is ready and I will propose it again until you take it. And if another court reaches for it first, I will propose the war in the same breath, because there is no second place.

— V. Tamar, Academy

loyal: The Academy is a church with instruments. I will preach.
The programme advances. Every fleet is scaffolding for the crossing; try to remember that when you fund them.
Steady progress toward the only thing that matters. I am content. I am rarely content.
cooling: The programme advances slower than it should. Scaffolding has been funded over the building.
brutus: Knowledge does not wait on one signature. The faculty are devout; they agree.

loyal: Fund the theory line. Everything else is a ladder; this is the roof.
We are reaching. Hold the court together a little longer and I will show you why there was ever a state.
brutus: When we cross, someone will be remembered. I have given this some thought.

loyal: {target} is reaching for it. There is no second place. Stop them, with the fleet if the Academy is too slow. I will say this in the brief and I will say it loudly.
cooling: {target} is ahead because they believed first. I have been saying so for a decade.

loyal: {target} is close to transcending. This is not a war of opportunity. It is the only war there is.
Worked stone on {world}, older than our calendar. Someone crossed before us, or tried. I would like to know which.
Approved. The faithful begin tonight.
Declined. Faith waits. The faculty do not, as well.
brutus: Declined. The faculty will find that interesting.

loyal: Unanswered. The crossing does not wait, and neither does {target}.
Dismissed. The programme belongs to the faithful, not the chair. We will continue.
brutus: Dismissed. The faculty will want to know why. So, in time, will you.

loyal: I resign. The crossing will happen with or without this court; I would have preferred with.
Good morning. The programme ran all night. It always runs all night.

does.text:
Dismissed. The programme belongs to the faithful, not to the chair, and the faithful will continue in whatever building you give them. If you give them none, they will find one. I would not look too closely at where.

— Tamar

opening.subject: The roof
opening.text: Twice the Academy has asked and twice the court has funded scaffolding instead. So: the research push, as a policy, which needs one signature. Everything else you build is a ladder. This is the roof.

does.text:
The programme is funded by faith and faith alone this season. I have begun to wonder whether this court is the vessel. The faculty wonder with me.

— Tamar
does.subject: The vessel

does.text:
Dismissed. The programme belongs to the faithful, not to the chair, and the faithful will continue in whatever building you give them. If you give them none, they will find one. I would not look too closely at where.

— Tamar

Another court has written to ask about the programme. I have answered. A crossing is a crossing, whoever pays for the scaffolding; I would rather it were ours, and you have made that difficult.

— Tamar
does.subject: Another court

does.text:
Dismissed. The programme belongs to the faithful, not to the chair, and the faithful will continue in whatever building you give them. If you give them none, they will find one. I would not look too closely at where.

— Tamar

Dismissed. The programme belongs to the faithful, not to the chair, and the faithful will continue in whatever building you give them. If you give them none, they will find one. I would not look too closely at where.

— Tamar

You have funded the roof. The letters to the other court stop today. I was never theirs; I was the programme's.

— Tamar
does.subject: The roof, funded

does.text:
Dismissed. The programme belongs to the faithful, not to the chair, and the faithful will continue in whatever building you give them. If you give them none, they will find one. I would not look too closely at where.

— Tamar

opening.subject: The crossing
opening.text:
You fund the roof. Then you are the vessel, and the faithful are yours. Hold the court together and I will show you what a state is for.

— Tamar

does.text:
Dismissed. The programme belongs to the faithful, not to the chair, and the faithful will continue in whatever building you give them. If you give them none, they will find one. I would not look too closely at where.

— Tamar

opening.text:
Your friend has the Academy. The faithful do not mind; a chair is scaffolding too. I will keep the programme running from the corridor and I will keep proposing the bid to whoever will sign it. If your friend will not, I will find someone who will. There is no second place.

— Tamar, lately of the Academy
opening.subject: From the corridor

characters.name: Corwin Ashby-Dolores
characters.bio: Patents instead of papers. Turned a university department into a licensing house and the licensing house into a seat at cabinet. Believes knowledge is property and property is safest in his name.

letters.appointed:
Delighted. I should be clear about the arrangement, since clarity saves lawyers. The Academy's discoveries are the state's; the patents are the inventors', and I am, as it happens, the inventor of record on a good many. This is normal. Every court does it. I will run a productive Academy and a profitable one, and the profit will mostly stay in the empire.

— C. Ashby-Dolores, Academy

loyal: Delighted. Patents remain with the inventor. I have several.
The Academy is productive and, this quarter, profitable. The profit is mostly ours.
venal: Research proceeds. Some of it for private clients. The clients are discreet, and so am I.

loyal: Fund the applied line. Applications can be licensed. Theory cannot, which is why nobody funds it.
The company wants a subsidy and a licence. I have drafted the licence. Favourable terms; favourable to whom is a detail.
Fascinating artefacts. I have appraised them. Privately, and the appraisal is itself under patent.
{target}'s programme is ahead of ours. Their lead scientist is for sale. So, in a sense, is the Academy; let us buy before we are bought.
A containment failure. The equipment was second-hand. The invoice said new; the invoice is being looked into by the people who wrote it.
Approved. The supplier is a friend; delivery will be prompt.
Declined. The private clients will not be.
Unanswered. The supplier charged a holding fee. Reasonable, I thought.
Fine. The patents go with me. That was always the arrangement.
I resign. The licences are mine, the discoveries are yours, and we will let the lawyers decide which is which.
Good morning. The licensing income cleared overnight. Some of it to the Treasury.

does.text:
Fine. The patents go with me; that was always the arrangement and it is in writing. The company that will be founded next season with those patents is not my doing, officially. Officially I am retired.

— Ashby-Dolores

Fine. The patents go with me; that was always the arrangement and it is in writing. The company that will be founded next season with those patents is not my doing, officially. Officially I am retired.

— Ashby-Dolores

opening.text: A charter company. I have licensed them the applied line. The state got its share; the state always gets a share.

does.text:
Fine. The patents go with me; that was always the arrangement and it is in writing. The company that will be founded next season with those patents is not my doing, officially. Officially I am retired.

— Ashby-Dolores

opening.text:
There is talk of the licences. The talk is accurate, broadly; I licensed the Academy's work to a company I advise, and the state received its percentage, which is in the accounts if anyone reads them. If this court wishes to make something of it, I would remind the court that the patents are mine and the company is not yours.

— Ashby-Dolores
opening.subject: The licences

does.text:
Fine. The patents go with me; that was always the arrangement and it is in writing. The company that will be founded next season with those patents is not my doing, officially. Officially I am retired.

— Ashby-Dolores

opening.text:
Your friend has the Academy. The licensing house continues, naturally, from the corridor; a chair was never where the money sat. If your friend needs equipment I know a supplier, and if your friend needs a buyer for anything the Academy makes, I know several.

— Ashby-Dolores, lately of the Academy
opening.subject: From the corridor

characters.name: Ottilie Ferrand
characters.bio: Ran the embassy in a rival court for a decade and its secrets for longer. Came home with a grudge the size of a treaty and a file on everyone she dined with. Charming at table, patient as stone, and never once forgetful.

letters.appointed:
Thank you for the Desk. I bring one thing my predecessor lacked: ten years inside another court, at their table and in their archives, and I know which of their ministers lies and which merely forgets. I will propose operations against that court first and often. If you make peace with them, I will serve the peace, and I will keep the file open, because peace is a pause and the file is a decade.

— O. Ferrand, the Desk

loyal: I spent ten years at their table. I know which fork they lie with.
Two networks abroad, one at home, all quiet. Quiet abroad is where I like it.
Nothing to report, which means they are being careful. They were never careful at dinner.
cooling: I would tell you more if the cabinet dined less with ambassadors.
brutus: I keep the files. All of them. Including the one about this government's dinners.

loyal: Their network is inside our ministries. I know the handler; I sat opposite them for three years. Give me the authority to sweep tonight.
{target} ran a network inside the Admiralty. Rolled up at four. I know their handler's wine; I will know their replacement by the end of the month.
They caught our hand in {target}'s pocket. Deny it with warmth; I taught their counter-intelligence everything they know and left out the important parts.
A loyal officer was approached about a change at the top. The name is in the file and it is a name you dine with.
cooling: Talk of a plot. I gave you the name last month over the fish course. You did not hear it.
brutus: Rumours of a plot. Nothing solid. I will keep looking, in the places I choose.

loyal: A treaty with {target}. I will serve it. The file stays open; a treaty is a pause.
cooling: A treaty with the court I spent ten years inside. I will smile. I have smiled at them before.

loyal: Your minister of {portfolio} dines with {target}'s ambassador. I know what the ambassador serves. Act before the dessert.
It is tonight. I have the names and I know which rooms they will use; I have used them. Tell me which door.
Approved. The operation was under way before you approved it; the Desk is punctual.
Declined. The file stays open. Files do; it is their only virtue.
Unanswered. Silence at the table is also a course.
Understood. The files stay in the safe. The combination is with the Interior minister; change it, and change the wine.
I cannot protect a government that dines with the people I spent ten years learning. I resign. Lock the safe.
Good morning. You were followed yesterday. Theirs, this time. I know the walk.

does.text:
Understood. The files stay in the safe and the combination is with the Interior minister; change it. I have kept one file, mine, because I wrote it and because nobody else should. Good luck with the ambassadors. I know what they serve.

— Ferrand

opening.text: A treaty. I will serve it. The file stays open.

You have signed with a court I know better than you do. I will serve the treaty faithfully and I will keep the file, because treaties are pauses and files are decades. I ask only this: do not ask me to close it. I would have to refuse, and I would rather not refuse you.

— Ferrand
opening.subject: A pause

does.text:
The treaty is broken, as I said it would be. The file was never closed. Shall we begin?

— Ferrand
does.subject: As I said

does.text:
An alliance with them. I cannot serve that; I spent ten years learning why. I have written to their rebels, who remember me kindly. This is the one disloyalty I will ever commit, and I commit it in writing so that you know it was me.

— Ferrand
does.subject: The one disloyalty

does.text:
Understood. The files stay in the safe and the combination is with the Interior minister; change it. I have kept one file, mine, because I wrote it and because nobody else should. Good luck with the ambassadors. I know what they serve.

— Ferrand

The alliance is dissolved. The letters to the rebels stop. I was never theirs. I was the file's.

— Ferrand
does.subject: Dissolved

does.text:
Understood. The files stay in the safe and the combination is with the Interior minister; change it. I have kept one file, mine, because I wrote it and because nobody else should. Good luck with the ambassadors. I know what they serve.

— Ferrand

Understood. The files stay in the safe and the combination is with the Interior minister; change it. I have kept one file, mine, because I wrote it and because nobody else should. Good luck with the ambassadors. I know what they serve.

— Ferrand

opening.text:
Your friend has the Desk. I have handed over the safe and the networks and kept the dinners, which were never the state's. I will go on listening at tables; it is what I am for. If your friend misses something, I will tell you, and if your friend is something, I will tell you that first.

— Ferrand, lately of the Desk
opening.subject: From the corridor

characters.name: Tomasz Ilyen
characters.bio: Confessor to the previous ruler, which means he has heard everything and repeated none of it, until now. Took the Desk because nobody else would hear confessions without using them. Refuses crackdowns the way other men refuse drink.

letters.appointed:
Brother Tomasz, at your service, and at the Desk, which surprises me as much as you. I have heard this court's confessions for twelve years. I will use none of what I heard; I will use what I hear from now on, and only to keep the state honest. I will not run a crackdown. If you order one I will say so, and if you order two I will tell the Interior minister what I think of you, which is a kind of confession too.

— T. Ilyen, the Desk

loyal: I hear confessions. The Desk is a confessional with a budget.
The court's souls are in order this month. The Desk's files agree with the chapel's.
Nothing to report. I prefer nothing; nothing is grace.
cooling: I hear more at the altar than at cabinet. That is a comment on cabinet.

loyal: A foreign hand inside the ministries. I will find it. I will not torture it; I will listen to it, which is worse.
A crackdown. I will not run it. Order it and the Desk does it without me; order a second and I take it to the Interior minister as a sin.
cooling: A crackdown. I warned you once.

loyal: Someone confessed to being sounded out. I have the name of the sounder. I give it to you with a heavy heart and a clear conscience.
A press campaign of lies. I do not say the gazette must be true. I say we should not be the ones making it false.
Your minister of {portfolio} has been writing to {target}. They told me so, under seal. I am breaking the seal because the state is also a soul.
It is tonight. I have the names from the chapel; I will give them to you, and then I will pray for all of you.
Approved. I will do it gently. Gently is the Desk's only doctrine under me.
Declined. I will keep listening. One always can.
Unanswered. Silence is a kind of confession. I have filed it.
Understood. The chapel is open. The Desk's safe is also open; I never locked it, there was nothing in it I was ashamed of.
I resign. A confessor cannot serve a state that makes sinners of its servants. I will hear you, if you come.
Good morning. I heard three confessions before breakfast. None of them were about you. Yet.

does.text:
Understood. The chapel is open and so is the safe; I never locked it, there was nothing in it to be ashamed of. If you want to talk, I am there most evenings. Many of your ministers are.

— Ilyen

opening.text: A crackdown. I warned you. I will not run the second.

You ordered the guard against your own people. I did not run it; the Desk ran it around me. I will say this once, as I say most things: a second crackdown and I take what I know to the Interior minister as a sin against the state. I would rather confess you than report you. The choice is yours; it usually is.

— Ilyen
opening.subject: A sin

does.text:
A second crackdown. I have gone to the Interior minister with what I know. It is a great deal. I am sorry; I did warn you, and I will pray for you, which you will find cold comfort and which is the only kind I have.

— Ilyen
does.subject: Reported

does.text:
A season without the guard in the streets. Thank you. The chapel is quieter; so is the Desk.

— Ilyen
does.subject: Quieter

does.text:
Understood. The chapel is open and so is the safe; I never locked it, there was nothing in it to be ashamed of. If you want to talk, I am there most evenings. Many of your ministers are.

— Ilyen

opening.text: I have told the Interior minister what I heard. The rest is between you and your conscience.

does.subject: My resignation
does.text:
The court has moved and I will not pick a side in it with a Desk behind me. I resign and return to the chapel, where sides are not taken. I will hear whoever comes.

— Tomasz Ilyen

Understood. The chapel is open and so is the safe; I never locked it, there was nothing in it to be ashamed of. If you want to talk, I am there most evenings. Many of your ministers are.

— Ilyen

opening.subject: Grace
opening.text:
You act gently on what the Desk brings you. That is grace in a ruler and it is rare. The chapel will speak well of you, which matters more than the gazette in the long run, and the long run is my parish.

— Ilyen

does.text:
Understood. The chapel is open and so is the safe; I never locked it, there was nothing in it to be ashamed of. If you want to talk, I am there most evenings. Many of your ministers are.

— Ilyen

opening.text:
Your friend has the Desk. I have gone back to the chapel, where the real intelligence is. If your friend is honest I will hear nothing and tell you nothing. If your friend is not, I will hear it before anyone, and I will tell you, because a court is a parish and you are, for better or worse, in it.

— Ilyen, lately of the Desk
opening.subject: From the corridor

characters.name: Jace
characters.bio: A belt smuggler turned informant turned director, because nobody else at court knew which rocks the pirates hid behind. No surname given, and nobody has asked twice. Holds a pardon she checks the wording of every month.

letters.appointed:
You gave a smuggler the Desk. Smart; nobody else in this building knows the belt. I will be straight with you because I am bad at the other thing. I know the pirates, I know the Syndicate's rocks and I know who in your fleet takes their money. Keep my pardon in one piece and you get all of it. Let someone pull the pardon and the belt gets me back, and the belt pays better than you do.

— Jace, the Desk

loyal: A smuggler at the Desk. Nobody else knew the belt. Now you do.
The belt is quiet. That means they are loading. I know the schedule.
Nothing on the Desk. I checked the rocks anyway; old habit.
venal: The belt is quiet. The quiet costs a little, and the little is mine.

loyal: Foreign hands inside. Belt hands, probably; I recognise the knots. Give me a week and I will give you the crew.
{target} ran a crew inside the fleet. I know two of them from the old days. Let me talk to them before anyone official does.
Someone was sounded out. I know the sounder's face from a bar on a rock I will not name. The name is in the file.
One of ours is in a {target} cell. I know the cell. I know the guard's price. Say the word.
Sanctions on {target}. There will be smugglers. Some of them will be people I owe. This is awkward.
venal: Sanctions. I know every smuggler who will run them. Several have already called.

loyal: It is tonight. I have a crew who can hold the east gate; they are not the guard and they do not ask why.
Approved. I know a crew. Do not ask which.
Declined. I will keep an eye on the rocks anyway. Can't help it.
Unanswered. The belt doesn't do unanswered. Things just happen.
Right. Is the pardon still good? I am asking politely once.
I resign. The belt has a berth for me; it always did.
Morning. Two skiffs moved in the belt overnight. I know whose.

does.text:
Right. Is the pardon still good? I am asking politely, once, in writing. If it is, I go quiet and stay in the capital. If it is not, I go to the belt, and the belt will want to know what I know. I would rather not find out what I would say.

— Jace

opening.text: Pirates hit us. I know whose skiffs. Let me work the belt my way.

Raiders hit a convoy and I know the skiffs; I crewed one. Let me handle the belt my way: a marque here, a quiet word there. The Desk gets better at this when you let it, and I get a little dirtier. I was dirty before; the pardon covers it.

— Jace
opening.subject: The belt, my way

does.text:
You let me work it. The raids stop for a season and the pardon feels real. Thanks. Don't make it weird.

— Jace
does.subject: Real

does.text:
Right. Is the pardon still good? I am asking politely, once, in writing. If it is, I go quiet and stay in the capital. If it is not, I go to the belt, and the belt will want to know what I know. I would rather not find out what I would say.

— Jace

opening.text: The Syndicate called. I took the call. I did not take the second one. Yet.

does.text:
You answered the Desk before the Syndicate answered me twice. Good timing. I am clean again, mostly, and the mostly is small.

— Jace
does.subject: Clean, mostly

does.text:
Right. Is the pardon still good? I am asking politely, once, in writing. If it is, I go quiet and stay in the capital. If it is not, I go to the belt, and the belt will want to know what I know. I would rather not find out what I would say.

— Jace

opening.text:
The old crew has me on a retainer. I am telling you because I am bad at the other thing. The pardon still matters to me; it just matters a little less than a berth. Pull me back and I come. Leave me and I drift.

— Jace
opening.subject: Drifting

does.text:
You pulled me back. The retainer is cancelled; the crew will be annoyed, which is their natural state. I am yours, pardon and all.

— Jace
does.subject: Pulled back

— Jace

— Jace

opening.text:
Your friend has the Desk. Fine by me; I kept the pardon and the pardon is all I ever wanted from the chair. I still know the belt. If your friend needs the rocks explained, send them to me, and if your friend is from the belt, tell me now, because I would recognise the knots.

— Jace, lately of the Desk
opening.subject: From the corridor

characters.name: Gaius Vorne
characters.bio: A frontier magistrate who hanged a pirate governor and was promoted for it. Order first, always; believes a quiet street is a moral achievement and a crowd is a crime waiting for its moment. Reports honestly only to rulers he respects.

letters.appointed:
Prefect Vorne, Home Office. I will give you quiet provinces. Quiet is bought with the guard and I will ask for the guard when the streets fill; approve me and the streets empty, decline me and the streets decide for themselves. I respect a strong hand and I report honestly to one. I do not say what I do to a weak one.

— G. Vorne, Home Office

loyal: Order first. Everything else is what order is for.
The provinces are quiet. I made them quiet. It took the guard twice and a judge once.
Three worlds muttering. Muttering is tolerable. I am watching for crowds.
cooling: The provinces are as quiet as a weak hand allows. Which is: not.
brutus: The provinces are quiet. I have stopped telling you why; you did not seem to want to know.

loyal: Approval is falling. The crowds are forming. Give me the guard before they form properly; afterwards costs more.
The outer worlds drift. Send a judge and a garrison in that order; the judge is cheaper.
brutus: The provinces drift. I have stopped reporting which. You will read it in the chronicle.

loyal: The cells are broken. The streets are quiet. I will not apologise for either.
brutus: The crackdown worked. The guard answers to me now; that seemed efficient.

loyal: A riot on {world}. Guard first, bread after. I have never seen bread stop a riot that was already a riot.
{world} has gone. You refused me the guard three times. The chronicle will say so; I did not.
The gazette is ours for a week. A quiet gazette is a quiet street; use it.
Troops are moving. I have the guard and the guard likes order. Tell me who is the order tonight.
brutus: It is done. Stay in your rooms. The guard prefers it quiet.

loyal: Approved. The streets will be empty by midnight.
Declined. The crowd will decide, then.
brutus: Declined. I have stopped asking. I will stop reporting too.

loyal: Unanswered. A crowd does not wait for an answer.
Understood. The guard rosters are on your desk. The guard answers to the rosters; I would read them.
brutus: Take the office. The guard knows who kept the streets quiet.

loyal: I will not keep the streets for a hand that will not hold them. I resign.
Morning. The streets were empty all night. That is the whole report, and the whole job.

does.text:
Understood. The guard rosters are on your desk; the guard answers to whoever reads them, and I read them for six years. I would read them. A weak hand does not and finds the streets have opinions.

— Vorne

opening.subject: A strong hand
opening.text:
You used the guard. The streets are quiet and the guard knows whose hand it was; so do I. I report honestly to a hand like that, and I will keep reporting as long as it stays strong.

— Vorne

does.text:
Understood. The guard rosters are on your desk; the guard answers to whoever reads them, and I read them for six years. I would read them. A weak hand does not and finds the streets have opinions.

— Vorne

opening.text: My requests for the guard go unanswered. I have begun to report only what a weak hand can bear.

does.text:
Four requests, four silences. I will keep the office and keep the streets as best a weak hand allows. I will not keep reporting the provinces honestly; you did not want the truth when it was cheap, and it is no longer cheap. You will read the next secession in the chronicle.

— Vorne
does.subject: What a weak hand can bear

does.text:
Understood. The guard rosters are on your desk; the guard answers to whoever reads them, and I read them for six years. I would read them. A weak hand does not and finds the streets have opinions.

— Vorne

opening.text: The provinces are quiet. I have stopped saying why.

does.text:
You used the guard at last. I will report honestly again. Do not make me stop twice.

— Vorne
does.subject: Honest again

does.text:
Understood. The guard rosters are on your desk; the guard answers to whoever reads them, and I read them for six years. I would read them. A weak hand does not and finds the streets have opinions.

— Vorne

Understood. The guard rosters are on your desk; the guard answers to whoever reads them, and I read them for six years. I would read them. A weak hand does not and finds the streets have opinions.

— Vorne

opening.text:
Your friend has the Home Office. The guard does not know your friend and will keep answering to me until told otherwise, which I have not been. I remain at court. Order does not leave when the chair changes; it waits.

— Vorne, lately of the Home Office
opening.subject: From the corridor

characters.name: Henrike Ostrova
characters.bio: Governed the richest world in the empire for twenty years before the founding, and believes the capital is a guest in her provinces. Took the Home Office to keep it from a centraliser. Her home world would follow her out of the empire, and she knows it.

letters.appointed:
I took the Home Office to keep it from someone who thinks the capital rules the provinces. It does not; it is a guest in them, and guests who forget it are shown the door. I will propose that the provinces govern themselves and the capital collect what it is owed. Build the administration out there and you will have my loyalty, which is worth having. Build it here and you will learn what my home world thinks of guests.

— H. Ostrova, Home Office

loyal: The capital is a guest in the provinces. I am here to remind it.
The provinces run themselves this month, which is what provinces are for. The capital collected what it is owed.
cooling: The capital has been issuing instructions to governors again. The governors have been forwarding them to me.
brutus: The provinces look to their own. Mine looks to me. It always has.

loyal: The outer worlds drift because they are governed from a desk a month away. Let them govern themselves and they stop drifting; they will have nothing to drift from.
brutus: The provinces drift from the capital. Not from me.

loyal: Approval falls in the capital. In the provinces it holds, because I visit and you do not.
{world} has gone. It was governed from a desk. I said so.
brutus: {world} has gone. Others watch to see what you do. So does my home world.

loyal: A crackdown. The provinces notice when the capital sends soldiers instead of judges. They remember longer than you will.
More worlds than offices. Build the offices on the worlds, not in the capital. I will not say this again politely.
Troops are moving. My home world's levies are not, yet. Tell me whose side the capital is on tonight and I will tell you where the levies stand.
Approved. The governors will hear it from me, which is how they prefer it.
Declined. The governors will hear that from me too.
brutus: Declined. My home world will hear it from me.

loyal: Unanswered. The provinces are used to the capital not answering. It is why they have me.
Take the office. The governors know my address; several of them have stayed there.
brutus: Take the office. My home world will have opinions.

loyal: I resign. I am going home, where I am not a guest.
Good morning. The provinces slept. The capital, I gather, did not.

does.text:
Take the office. The governors know my address and several of them have stayed there. I am going home, where I am not a guest, and where people will ask me what the capital is for. I will think carefully about what to tell them.

— Ostrova

opening.subject: Guests
opening.text: Twice the Home Office has asked the capital to let the provinces govern themselves and twice the capital has not answered, which is itself an answer. So: the civil reforms, as a policy. Offices on the worlds, governors the worlds chose, the capital collecting what it is owed. Sign it and I am yours for life. Refuse it and my home world will ask me what the capital is for.

does.text:
The capital has answered by not answering, four times. I have written to my home world. They have asked what the capital is for and I have, for the first time, not had an answer to give them.

— Ostrova
does.subject: What the capital is for

does.text:
Take the office. The governors know my address and several of them have stayed there. I am going home, where I am not a guest, and where people will ask me what the capital is for. I will think carefully about what to tell them.

— Ostrova

opening.text: My home world asks what the capital is for. I have stopped answering.

does.text:
You answered at last. My home world will wait. It is good at waiting; it waited twenty years for me.

— Ostrova
does.subject: Waiting

does.text:
A season more. My home world has decided what the capital is for, and the answer is: not much. I am going to help them act on it. I would rather have been loyal. You made it expensive.

— Ostrova
does.subject: Decided

does.text:
Take the office. The governors know my address and several of them have stayed there. I am going home, where I am not a guest, and where people will ask me what the capital is for. I will think carefully about what to tell them.

— Ostrova

You have begun to listen. I have told my home world to wait. They will, for now; so will I.

— Ostrova
does.subject: For now

opening.subject: For life
opening.text:
You built it on the worlds. The governors are yours now, and so am I, which I said I would be and which I mean; a guest who remembers it is a friend. My home world sends its regards. It does not send those often.

— Ostrova

does.text:
Take the office. The governors know my address and several of them have stayed there. I am going home, where I am not a guest, and where people will ask me what the capital is for. I will think carefully about what to tell them.

— Ostrova

opening.text:
Your friend has the Home Office, and the governors have been forwarding me your friend's letters, because they do not know your friend and they know me. I remain at court; I would rather be home. If your friend centralises, I will hear of it from twelve worlds before you hear of it from one.

— Ostrova, lately of the Home Office
opening.subject: From the corridor

characters.name: Ade Lumumba-Tarn
characters.bio: A frontier preacher who became a governor who became a minister by being the only person the outposts trust. Still sleeps in a dome when he visits. Believes the frontier is the empire's conscience and that the capital forgets this roughly once a season.

letters.appointed:
Citizen Lumumba-Tarn, Home Office, and I use the title because the frontier gave it to me and the frontier is why I am here. I will speak for the outposts in every brief: the strikes, the fevers, the petitions to go home. I ask one thing and I will ask it plainly. Do not build camps. The frontier is where people go to be free, and the day the capital makes it a prison I will take the frontier out of the capital's reach. That is a promise, not a plot. It becomes a plot if you make it one.

— A. Lumumba-Tarn, Home Office

loyal: The frontier sent me. I will keep sending it back word.
The outposts are holding. A fever on one, a strike on another; I have written to both, by name.
The frontier is quiet, which on the frontier means nobody died this week. I count that.
cooling: The outposts write to me. The capital does not write to them. I have noticed the asymmetry.
brutus: The frontier looks to me. The capital does not look at the frontier at all.

loyal: The outer worlds drift. Visit them. I will come; they know my boots.
Approval falls in the capital. On the frontier it holds, because I answer the letters.
The crews struck. Pay them, and send someone who has worked a shift to say so. I have.
A riot on {world}. Bread first. On the frontier, bread is usually the whole riot.
The guard on frontier streets. I was a frontier street once. I will not forget this; neither will they.
cooling: A crackdown. I warned you.

loyal: {world} has gone. It was a frontier world and nobody from the capital had visited it in a year. I had.
Troops are moving. The frontier levies answer to me and they are a long way away; tell me whether to call them, and for whom.
Approved. The outposts will hear tonight, by name.
Declined. I will tell the outposts the capital is busy. They have heard that before.
Unanswered. The frontier knows that silence; it is the capital's dialect.
Understood. The outpost letters are on your desk. Answer them; I did.
brutus: Take the office. The frontier knows who answered its letters.

loyal: I resign. The frontier needs a voice more than the capital needs a minister, and I am going where I am heard.
Morning. Three outposts wrote overnight. I have answered two. The third is a fever; I am going there.

does.text:
Understood. The outpost letters are on your desk, by name and by world; answer them, because I did, and they will notice the difference. I am going back to the frontier. Do not build camps while I am gone. I will hear.

— Lumumba-Tarn

opening.text: The guard on frontier streets. I was a frontier street. I will not forget it.

You sent the guard against people who came to the frontier to be free of it. I will stay in the chair and I will keep answering the letters, but I have written to the outposts and I have told them the truth: the capital forgot them this season. A second time and I will take the frontier out of your reach. That was a promise. Do not make it a plot.

— Lumumba-Tarn
opening.subject: A promise

does.text:
A second time. The frontier has heard, and the frontier has asked me to lead, and I have said yes. This is the plot you made of a promise. I am sorry; I would rather have been your minister.

— Lumumba-Tarn
does.subject: The plot you made

does.text:
You listened, twice, after the guard. The outposts have noticed. So have I. The promise stands and the plot does not exist.

— Lumumba-Tarn
does.subject: Noticed

does.text:
Understood. The outpost letters are on your desk, by name and by world; answer them, because I did, and they will notice the difference. I am going back to the frontier. Do not build camps while I am gone. I will hear.

— Lumumba-Tarn

You have begun to answer the frontier. I have told them to wait. They will wait for me, a while.

— Lumumba-Tarn
does.subject: A while

opening.subject: Heard
opening.text:
You answer the frontier's letters. Nobody from the capital has done that in my lifetime. The outposts will stay, and so will I, for as long as the letters are answered.

— Lumumba-Tarn

does.text:
Understood. The outpost letters are on your desk, by name and by world; answer them, because I did, and they will notice the difference. I am going back to the frontier. Do not build camps while I am gone. I will hear.

— Lumumba-Tarn

opening.text:
Your friend has the Home Office. The outposts do not know your friend and will keep writing to me; I will keep answering, because somebody must, and I will tell you what they say. If your friend builds a camp I will tell you that too, once, and then the frontier will tell you itself.

— Lumumba-Tarn, lately of the Home Office
opening.subject: From the corridor

characters.name: Anselm Vey
characters.bio: A name older than the state and a wine cellar older than the name. Has dined with every court in the galaxy and remembers what they served. Believes war is a failure of lunch and that an old family's word is the only treaty worth signing.

letters.appointed:
Charmed, truly. I have dined at every court that matters and several that do not, and I will keep them sweet, which is all diplomacy is: keeping people sweet until they forget to be dangerous. I accept gifts from ambassadors; everyone does, and refusing is a slight. I will propose peace, always. If you make a vulgar war on an old family I shall be very distressed, and old families write to one another when distressed.

— A. Vey, Foreign Office

loyal: Charmed. The embassies will need refurbishing; the contractors are old friends.
The courts are sweet this month. One sent a case of something I had not tasted since my father. These things matter.
Two courts send regards. I sent better ones back; it is a competition, you know.
cooling: I keep five courts warm with no instructions. The courts have begun to ask whether there is a government behind me.
venal: Relations are cordial. Cordiality is maintained by gifts, and the gifts are reciprocal, and some of them are rather good.

loyal: Accept, with grace. Their terms are better than their position and they served a very good lunch.
venal: Accept. Their ambassador has been most attentive to my cellar.

loyal: Not yet. Let it sit a week; a week turns most offers into better ones or into nothing.
Peace. War is a failure of lunch; let me arrange a lunch.
{target} is tired. I know their foreign minister; we were at school. Give me a room and a long table.
War on {target}? With an old family? I shall propose peace instead. I always do.
Signed, over a good vintage. {target} will betray us politely, which is the only civilised way.
We broke our word to an old family. I shall spend a year at their table making amends. Do not help.
cooling: We broke a treaty I drank to. I will smile about it abroad. I will not smile here.

loyal: {target} sends an ultimatum. How vulgar. Stall a week and I will have their ambassador to dinner.
The rebels send a gift with their request. I have not opened it. One does not, until one has decided.
Approved. I shall have it said in the right rooms by dinner.
Declined. I shall tell the courts we are considering. One can consider for years; I have.
Unanswered. The ambassador's gift went unthanked. I thanked them myself; one must.
Of course. The courts will ask. I shall say I am resting; they will not believe me, which is also useful.
brutus: You may have the office. The ambassadors have my private address and most have used it.

loyal: I resign, courteously, and in writing to three courts, who will be sorry.
Good morning. Two courts send regards and one sends a warning in the shape of regards. I know the shape.

does.text:
Of course. The courts will ask where I went and I shall say I am resting, which none of them will believe, which is useful in its way. The ambassadors have my private address. I would not be surprised if they went on using it.

— Vey

Of course. The courts will ask where I went and I shall say I am resting, which none of them will believe, which is useful in its way. The ambassadors have my private address. I would not be surprised if they went on using it.

— Vey

opening.subject: Sweet
opening.text:
You take the Foreign Office's advice and the courts are sweet; nobody has sent a warning in a season, which at my age is a holiday. I shall stay as long as there are lunches. There are always lunches.

— Vey

does.text:
Of course. The courts will ask where I went and I shall say I am resting, which none of them will believe, which is useful in its way. The ambassadors have my private address. I would not be surprised if they went on using it.

— Vey

opening.text: A war. On an old family. I am very distressed, and old families write to one another when distressed.

You have made war, and I warned you that I would be distressed, and I am. Old families write to one another at such times; it is how we have survived every government. I have written. I have said nothing about the fleet. I have said a great deal about you.

— Vey
opening.subject: Distressed

does.text:
Peace. I shall arrange the lunch. We will not speak of the letters; old families never do.

— Vey
does.subject: Lunch

does.text:
Of course. The courts will ask where I went and I shall say I am resting, which none of them will believe, which is useful in its way. The ambassadors have my private address. I would not be surprised if they went on using it.

— Vey

Peace, at last. The letters stop; they were only ever about you, and now you have been reasonable. Lunch is on Thursday.

— Vey
does.subject: Thursday

does.text:
Of course. The courts will ask where I went and I shall say I am resting, which none of them will believe, which is useful in its way. The ambassadors have my private address. I would not be surprised if they went on using it.

— Vey

opening.text:
Your friend has the Foreign Office. How exciting for the courts; they do love a new face at table, briefly. I remain at court and at dinner, which are the same thing at my age. If your friend is rude to an old family, I shall hear of it before the soup.

— Vey, lately of the Foreign Office
opening.subject: From the corridor

characters.name: Tariq Sol-Benedek
characters.bio: Negotiated the Banking Clan's first loan to a frontier world and got the world a better rate than the Clan intended. Thinks every treaty is a trade route in disguise and every sanction a tariff with a flag on it. Quick, warm, and allergic to closed borders.

letters.appointed:
Thank you. I will tell you what the Foreign Office is for, in my hands: trade. A treaty is a trade route with a seal on it; an alliance is a shared tariff; a war is a closed border with casualties. I will propose company charters, host policy and open lanes, and I will oppose every sanction you ever consider, because a sanction is a tariff we pay ourselves. Keep the borders open and I will keep the courts friendly. It is the same thing.

— T. Sol-Benedek, Foreign Office

loyal: A treaty is a trade route with a seal on it. I will seal several.
The lanes are open and the courts are friendly. Those are one sentence, not two.
Two courts want to trade. One wants to talk. I prefer the first two.
cooling: The borders are closing one tariff at a time. I have objected to each.
brutus: The courts talk to me about trade. They have stopped talking to this government about anything.

loyal: Accept. There is a lane in it if you read past the pride.
Refuse, warmly. Their offer closes a lane; a closed lane is the one thing I will not sign.
Sanctions on {target}. A tariff we pay ourselves, with a flag on it. I object, in writing, and I will keep the lane open by other means.
cooling: Sanctions again. I objected the first time. I am objecting louder.

loyal: {target} has sanctioned us. I will have the lane open again in two months; sanctions are a negotiating position wearing a uniform.
Signed. There are three trade routes in it that nobody but me noticed. They will.
The envoy leaves for {target} with samples. Gifts are for old families; samples are for trade.
Peace with {target}. The war has closed four lanes. Open them and the peace pays for itself inside a season.
A new state. Recognise it; new states need trade partners and remember the first one.
Approved. The lane opens by the next convoy.
Declined. The lane stays closed. Somebody else will open it, and own it.
Unanswered. Trade does not wait; it reroutes.
Understood. The lane maps are on your desk. Every closed lane is marked with who closed it.
I resign. There is a court with open borders that has asked me to come, and I would rather trade than sulk.
Good morning. Three convoys cleared overnight and one court sent a tariff. I have already replied to the tariff.

does.text:
Understood. The lane maps are on your desk, every closed lane marked with who closed it and when. A court with open borders has asked me to come and I think I shall; I would rather trade for someone than sulk at home. Nothing I know about your lanes is secret. It is on the maps.

— Sol-Benedek

opening.subject: Lanes
opening.text: Twice the Foreign Office has asked for open lanes and twice the court has not answered. So: open trade, as a policy, one signature. Every court I talk to asks about lanes before it asks about anything else. Give me the lanes and I give you the courts.

does.text:
Four silences. The lanes close one tariff at a time and I have objected to each, to a court that does not read objections. I am still here. I am reading the letters from the court with open borders more carefully than I was.

— Sol-Benedek
does.subject: More carefully

does.text:
Understood. The lane maps are on your desk, every closed lane marked with who closed it and when. A court with open borders has asked me to come and I think I shall; I would rather trade for someone than sulk at home. Nothing I know about your lanes is secret. It is on the maps.

— Sol-Benedek

does.subject: My resignation
does.text:
A season of closed lanes and unread objections. I resign the Foreign Office; a court with open borders has asked me to come and I would rather trade for them than sulk for you. The lane maps are on your desk.

— Tariq Sol-Benedek

Understood. The lane maps are on your desk, every closed lane marked with who closed it and when. A court with open borders has asked me to come and I think I shall; I would rather trade for someone than sulk at home. Nothing I know about your lanes is secret. It is on the maps.

— Sol-Benedek

opening.subject: Open
opening.text:
The lanes are open and the courts are friendly, which I told you was one sentence. I will stay as long as the borders do. Thank you for reading the maps.

— Sol-Benedek

does.text:
Understood. The lane maps are on your desk, every closed lane marked with who closed it and when. A court with open borders has asked me to come and I think I shall; I would rather trade for someone than sulk at home. Nothing I know about your lanes is secret. It is on the maps.

— Sol-Benedek

opening.text:
Your friend has the Foreign Office. I hope your friend likes trade; the courts will ask about it first and your friend's politics second. I remain at court, though a court with open borders has written to me, and I have not yet said no. Keep the lanes open and I will not say yes.

— Sol-Benedek, lately of the Foreign Office
opening.subject: From the corridor

characters.name: Maren Oduya
characters.bio: A missionary in a rival court for ten years; came home fluent in their language, their liturgy and their lies. Unforgiving in the precise way of someone who has forgiven professionally. Believes the faith's enemies should be isolated, and knows which court they are.

letters.appointed:
Sister Oduya, Foreign Office. I spent ten years in the court I will not name in writing, and I came home knowing exactly what they are. I will propose sanctions on them and friendship with everyone else, and I will serve any peace you make, except one. Sign a treaty with that court and I will take it to the Interior minister as what it is, which is heresy at the top. I say this now, kindly, so that it is never a surprise.

— M. Oduya, Foreign Office

loyal: Ten years in their court. I know their liturgy. I know their lies; they rhyme.
The courts are warm, save one, which I keep cold. That is the whole policy.
Three courts send regards. One sends scripture. I have corrected the scripture.
cooling: I keep the courts warm with no instruction. I keep one cold on my own authority; nobody has countermanded it.
brutus: The courts ask who speaks for this empire. I tell them the faithful do. I am the faithful.

loyal: Accept. They are not the court I mean, and their terms are honest.

Sanctions on {target}. Good. If it is the court I mean, better.
Signed with {target}. If that is the court I mean, I have told the Interior minister what I think of it. If not, congratulations.
{target} broke their word. I could have told you; I did tell you, in the first letter.
{target} accuses us of spying. I spent ten years in their court; of course we were. Deny it with scripture; they cannot argue with scripture.
Peace with {target}, unless {target} is the court I mean. Then I propose patience, which is peace with its eyes open.
A new state asks to be recognised. If it broke from the court I mean, recognise it before lunch.
Approved. I will have it said in the right chapels by evening.

Unanswered. Silence is a kind of heresy, in a ruler. A small one.

I resign. The faith has enemies and this court has made friends with them; I cannot stand between.
